states.changed: First state: the whole public record of AI incidents as one sheet of 1,803 paragraphs and 6,964 words, almost all of it grey type; 21 paragraphs begin in red handwriting where the person harmed wrote first, 50 end in a blue seal where a public body acted; a visitor can lift the type off, step through what remains, and let the sheet write itself from 1983 with keys, a pen and a stamp.

Second state: the seals are the Field's checked ones, 60 and not 50, whole where an act was concluded and half where it was only begun; a red line now runs through the press reports in which the harmed speak, and the second reading leaves every first report that anyone read; a drawn key stands above the sheet, and the counts below show the 52 first reports by the harmed that are estimated and were never found.

The check: the type is now small and the exceptions large, so the whole sheet stands on little more than one screen; a seal stands in the margin, left where the act lands on the person who used the AI and right where it concerns whoever made or ran it, a disc when concluded and a ring when only begun; read again, 30 of the 60 acts are concluded and not 34, and two acts on the right, drawn black, went in the maker's favour; a box under the sheet says what was checked, what held and what was corrected.

The presented state: the sheet now carries 69 seals and not 60, with the nine acts the Field found in public bodies' own first reports; a third black seal stands on the left, where a judge declined to sanction a man who filed invented citations; and eight seals have a red rim, where the act answers a claim the harmed brought, all eight on the right-hand side of their columns.

After the presentation, on the Atelier's two corrections: the red line now runs only where the harmed are quoted in their own words (47), a broken red line where they are only told by someone else (18), and three reports lost their line; the faint row of the estimated, never found reports runs on to 135 marks, each as faint as the estimate is unsure that so many exist, with ticks at 18, 52 and 135.
